title: Exterior Spray Painting

paragraphs: Spray painting is an application method, not a different kind of paint. It can suit broad walls and detailed profiles, but the material, coating instructions and site access determine whether spraying, brushing or rolling is the better choice.

Before spraying, we review windows, neighbouring properties, landscaping and parked vehicles. Masking and suitable wind conditions help control overspray. Some coatings and surfaces also need back-rolling or brushwork, so the finish method is confirmed for each area.
prepare: Clean off dirt and loose coating, prepare the substrate, and mask windows, fixtures and adjoining areas before spraying.
apply: Apply controlled passes with a suitable exterior coating; brush or back-roll when required by the product or surface.
condition: A sprayed finish cannot bond reliably to dirt, chalk or failing paint. Those issues need to be addressed first.
material: Siding, wood and masonry have different preparation and primer needs. The spray method must suit the selected coating.
goals: Identify the walls, trim and accents you want included so masking, access and application can be planned together.
